proposals.name: New Millage for Public Safety
proposals.description: Shall Alabaster-Township impose an increase of up to 0.500 mills ($0.50 per $1,000 of taxable value) in the tax limitation imposed under Article IX, Sec 6 of the Michigan Constitution and levy it for 5 years, 2027 through 2031 inclusive, to provide police protection and other public safety measures, which 0.500 mills increase will raise an estimated $34,500.00 in the first year the millage is levied.
proposals.ballotLanguage: Shall Alabaster-Township impose an increase of up to 0.500 mills ($0.50 per $1,000 of taxable value) in the tax limitation imposed under Article IX, Sec 6 of the Michigan Constitution and levy it for 5 years, 2027 through 2031 inclusive, to provide police protection and other public safety measures, which 0.500 mills increase will raise an estimated $34,500.00 in the first year the millage is levied.
proposals.yesVote: A YES vote approves a new levy of 0.5 mills for 5 years — this is a tax increase.
proposals.noVote: A NO vote rejects the new tax; your property tax rate stays where it is.
proposals.conservativeView: This is new taxation. Ask whether the need could be met within existing budgets, whether the millage sunsets, and who oversees how the money is spent.
proposals.progressiveView: New funding dedicated to a specific local service that supporters say current revenue cannot cover.

proposals.name: Mosquito Control and Suppression Millage
proposals.description: Shall the City of East Tawas be authorized to renew a previously authorized millage of 0.3909 mill ($0.3909 per $1,000 of taxable value), as reduced by the Headlee Amendment, levied upon the taxable value of all property in the City of East Tawas, County of Iosco, State of Michigan, for a period of five (5) years, 2028 through 2032, inclusive, for the sole purpose of providing mosquito control and suppression in the City of East Tawas, which renewal millage is projected to provide $45,000 in…
proposals.ballotLanguage: Shall the City of East Tawas be authorized to renew a previously authorized millage of 0.3909 mill ($0.3909 per $1,000 of taxable value), as reduced by the Headlee Amendment, levied upon the taxable value of all property in the City of East Tawas, County of Iosco, State of Michigan, for a period of five (5) years, 2028 through 2032, inclusive, for the sole purpose of providing mosquito control and suppression in the City of East Tawas, which renewal millage is projected to provide $45,000 in the first year of the levy, being 2028?
proposals.yesVote: A YES vote continues the existing levy of 0.3909 mills for 5 years — generally no increase over what you pay now.
proposals.noVote: A NO vote lets the current millage expire; the service it funds would need cuts or other revenue.
proposals.conservativeView: Renewals are the least disruptive way to keep a service funded, but every renewal is a chance to ask whether the service is delivering value. Watch for "renewal" proposals that quietly restore Headlee rollbacks — that is a tax increase.
proposals.progressiveView: Keeps an existing, voter-approved service funded at the same rate with no new tax.

proposals.name: Hale Area Schools Operating Millage Proposal
proposals.description:
This proposal will allow the school district to levy the statutory rate of not to exceed 18 mills on all property, except principal residence and other property exempted by law, required for the school district to receive its revenue per pupil foundation allowance.
Shall the limitation on the amount of taxes which may be assessed against all property, except principal residence and other property exempted by law, in Hale Area Schools, Iosco and Ogemaw Counties, Michigan, be increased by 2 mills…
proposals.ballotLanguage:
This proposal will allow the school district to levy the statutory rate of not to exceed 18 mills on all property, except principal residence and other property exempted by law, required for the school district to receive its revenue per pupil foundation allowance.
Shall the limitation on the amount of taxes which may be assessed against all property, except principal residence and other property exempted by law, in Hale Area Schools, Iosco and Ogemaw Counties, Michigan, be increased by 2 mills ($2.00 on each $1,000 of taxable valuation) for a period of 7 years, 2027 to 2033, inclusive, to provide funds for operating purposes; the estimate of the revenue the school district will collect if the millage is approved and levied in 2027 is approximately $131,490 (this millage is to restore millage lost as a result of the reduction required by the Michigan Constitution of 1963)?
proposals.officialTitle: HALE AREA SCHOOLS OPERATING MILLAGE PROPOSAL
proposals.yesVote: A YES vote raises the levy back to the originally authorized 18 mills, overriding the Headlee Amendment rollback — this is a tax increase over the current rate.
proposals.noVote: A NO vote keeps the current, rolled-back rate in place.
proposals.conservativeView: The Headlee Amendment is a constitutional taxpayer protection that limits how fast property-tax revenue can grow. Overriding it raises taxes above what the constitution would otherwise allow.
proposals.progressiveView: Restores funding that inflation and Headlee rollbacks have eroded so existing services can continue.
